name: Albania
fact: Declared in 2023, the Vjosa River National Park protects one of Europe's last wild, free-flowing rivers across its entire pristine ecosystem.

name: Andorra
fact: Nestled high in the Pyrenees mountains, this tranquil principality preserves the Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley, a breathtaking glacial UNESCO World Heritage landscape.

name: Austria
fact: Over three-quarters of the nation's electricity comes from renewable sources, propelled by extensive Alpine hydroelectric stations and expanding wind energy.

name: Belarus
fact: Sprawling across the southwestern border, the ancient Belovezhskaya Pushcha primeval forest shelters the continent's largest thriving population of wild European bison.

name: Belgium
fact: Renowned globally for master chocolatiers, Belgian artisans invented the filled praline in 1912 and continue to produce world-class gourmet confections.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
fact: Deep within Sutjeska National Park lies Perućica, one of Europe's rarest preserved primeval rainforests featuring towering centuries-old trees and cascading waterfalls.

name: Bulgaria
fact: Cultivated in the sunlit Rose Valley, Bulgaria's fragrant damask roses yield prized pure attar utilized by the world's finest luxury perfumeries.

name: Croatia
fact: Plitvice Lakes National Park enchants visitors with sixteen stepped crystalline lakes connected by dramatic waterfalls pouring through natural travertine dams.

name: Czechia
fact: Boasting more than two thousand castles, châteaux, and fortress ruins, the country preserves an extraordinary density of architectural heritage spanning several centuries.

name: Denmark
fact: Pioneering commercial wind power since the 1970s, Denmark generates over half of its annual electricity from offshore and onshore wind turbines.

name: Estonia
fact: Nearly ninety-nine percent of public services are accessible online twenty-four hours a day, establishing the nation as a global leader in digital innovation.

name: Finland
fact: Endowed with vast pristine wilderness, Finland encompasses approximately one hundred and eighty-eight thousand freshwater lakes, earning its reputation as the land of lakes.

name: France
fact: UNESCO inscribed the multi-course French gastronomic meal on its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in recognition of its rich culinary rituals and social togetherness.

name: Germany
fact: Centuries of careful sustainable woodland management have enabled lush forests to cover almost one-third of the nation's total land area today.

name: Greece
fact: Perched dramatically atop colossal natural sandstone monoliths, the historic Eastern Orthodox monasteries of Meteora offer awe-inspiring views and remarkable architectural mastery.

name: Hungary
fact: Heated by subterranean geothermal springs, Lake Hévíz constitutes the largest biologically active, swimmable thermal lake anywhere in the world.

name: Iceland
fact: Harnessing volcanic heat and glacial cascades, the island nation produces virtually all of its domestic electricity and home heating through renewable energy.

name: Ireland
fact: Rising sheer above the pounding Atlantic surf, the majestic Cliffs of Moher provide a sanctuary for over twenty distinct seabird species.

name: Italy
fact: Celebrated for timeless architecture and artistic genius, Italy safeguards sixty UNESCO World Heritage sites spanning ancient classical ruins to magnificent Renaissance cathedrals.
